frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: six spectral windows of 960 channels, 244.141 kHz width (~0.6 km/s), covering 129.538-132.405 GHz; one 2 GHz continuum window centred at 130.973 GHz (128 channels of 15.625 MHz)

evidence.quote: six spectral windows each of 960 channels with a channel width used during the observations of 244.141 kHz (about 0.6 km s$^{-1}$) covering about 1.4 GHz between 129.538 GHz and 132.405 GHz
emitting at 129671.82 MHz
c-C$_3$H$_2$ (3-2) line emission at 145089.6 MHz
with 39 antennas and baselines from 15.1 m (6.5 k$\lambda$) up to 713.1 m (310.0 k$\lambda$)
The resulting synthesized beam sizes are 1.28$\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ 1.00$\ensuremath{''}$ at a P.A.$\sim$ $-$89$\ensuremath{^\circ}$
with an on source time of about 39 min with ALMA, during Cycle 3.
The observations were performed toward TW Hya on 2016 May 31 and on 2016 June 1

analysis_steps.goal: Extract disk-averaged spectrum and confirm detection

method.value: Elliptical aperture of ~400 au on native data plus pixel spectral stacking

evidence.quote: disk-averaged spectrum extracted from the native dataset using an elliptical aperture of about 400 au

validation.value: Two independent methods above 4 sigma; line is the brightest expected in range

evidence.quote: two independent methods show a detection above the 4$\sigma$ level

analysis_steps.goal: Apply Keplerian mask and make integrated map

method.value: Keplerian mask, integrate v=0.9-3.4 km/s, smooth by 7"x7" Gaussian

evidence.quote: integrated over the line profile, from v=0.9 to 3.4 km s$^{-1}$ and smoothed by a Gaussian kernel of 7$\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ 7$\ensuremath{''}$

key_parameters.value: M*=0.7 Msun, i=7 deg, PA=155 deg, vsys=2.7 km/s, d=59 pc, Rout=400 au

evidence.quote: outer radius of 400 au (to be consistent with the data).
Assuming that the disk is in Keplerian rotation

validation.value: Mask checked on c-C3H2 (3-2) detected above 12 sigma; S/N improved by factor ~5

evidence.quote: the signal to noise ratio was enhanced by a factor $\sim$5.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive column density and HCOOH/CH3OH ratio

method.value: Convert disk-averaged integrated intensity to column density for Tex = 10 and 40 K; compare with methanol

evidence.quote: corresponds to a t-HCOOH source averaged column density of (2.9$\pm$1.3)$\times$10$^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$ and (3.5$\pm$0.8)$\times$10$^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$ for an excitation temperature of 10 and 40 K, respectively.
The 10-40 K temperature range is the typical one where the molecular gas is expected to be emissive.

analysis_steps.goal: Model HCOOH chemistry and synthetic observation

findings_qualitative.value: HCOOH is the first organic molecule with two oxygen atoms detected in a protoplanetary disk.

evidence.quote: HCOOH is the first organic molecules containing two oxygen atoms detected in a protoplanetary disk

claims.hypothesis: Is HCOOH detectable in the TW Hya disk?
claims.experiment: ALMA band 3 spectrum extraction, pixel stacking and Keplerian-mask analysis
claims.result: Line detected at S/N ~4 in the spectrum and 12 sigma after masking and smoothing
claims.finding: First detection of formic acid in a protoplanetary disk

evidence.quote: We detected the 129 GHz HCOOH line with a signal-to-noise ratio of about 4.

claims.hypothesis: Is HCOOH as abundant as methanol in the disk?
claims.experiment: Compared column densities with literature methanol
claims.finding: Abundance comparable to methanol, though spatial scales differ

evidence.quote: namely as large as that of methanol

claims.hypothesis: Can grain-surface formation with reactive desorption explain the HCOOH abundance?
claims.experiment: Disk chemical model with LIME synthetic observation
claims.result: Observed column densities reproduced within a factor 3
claims.finding: Chemical desorption model is consistent with observations

evidence.loc: 4.3 Chemical desorption as the source of HCOOH in disks?
evidence.quote: Our physico-chemical modeling reproduces well the observed column densities within a factor 3

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gas-phase ethanol-based scheme (Skouteris 2018) does not appear to dominate HCOOH production in a preliminary 0D model

evidence.loc: 4.3 Chemical desorption as the source of HCOOH in disks?
evidence.quote: this new set of reactions does not seem to dominate the production of formic acid in disks.

limitations_admitted.value: Low spatial and spectral resolution prevents resolving the emission structure and kinematics; at least 100 au uncertainty in spatial extent

evidence.quote: the low angular resolution observations along with the convolution procedure, lead to at least 100 au of uncertainty regarding the spatial extent of HCOOH.

limitations_admitted.value: Non-LTE not possible because HCOOH collisional rates are unavailable

evidence.quote: Non-LTE calculations could not be performed as the collisional rate coefficients for HCOOH are not available.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single line at S/N ~4 in the unmasked spectrum; the identification rests on the mask and stacking
Column density depends on an assumed emitting area and Tex
Methanol ratio compares different spatial scales
The Keplerian mask could bias the S/N

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project 2015.1.00845.S is cited with PI, so it is in the archive

evidence.quote: ADS/ JAO.ALMA$\#$2015.1.00845.S (PI C. Favre).

reproducibility.score_reason: Data are archival and the Keplerian mask parameters are given, but the imaging and self-calibration details and the column density derivation are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe incomplete, with a marginal detection that is sensitive to unstated imaging details.
